metadata.Syllabus Name: Data Science - Capstone Project_Dự án KHDL
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study;
metadata.Description:
This capstone project course is designed to consolidate and apply students' knowledge in data science to tackle real-world challenges. The course emphasizes:
- The application of data science techniques to solve practical problems.
- The identification and adaptation of data science methodologies from current research for specific problems.
- The development of a comprehensive solution approach using data science.
- The evaluation and analysis of results from data science projects.
- Recognition of appropriate scenarios for data science applications.
- Selection of suitable metrics for project evaluation.
- Understanding the ethical and legal implications of data handling.
- Implementation and reflection on various data science algorithms including preprocessing, machine learning models, and advanced analytical techniques.
- Effective teamwork and project management.
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Select a suitable project and form teams.
- Allocate and schedule tasks among team members.
- Develop a project output that meets the specified requirements and demonstrates individual contributions.
- Present and defend the project in front of a review
metadata.Tools:
- Programming Languages: Python, R
- Software Tools: Jupyter Notebook, TensorFlow, Scikit-Learn, Pandas
- Databases and Datasets: Kaggle, UCI Machine Learning Repository, Government databases
- Additional Resources: Google Scholar for research papers, GitHub for code repositories
metadata.Note:
"- The essential capstone project is mandatory, focusing on solving a real-world data challenge. It comprises 100% of assessments, culminating in a final exam by oral presentation.
- The final mark is determined by summing the weighted scores of Report 1 (10%), Report 2 (20%), Report 3 (40%), Final Report (10%), and Final Exam[Oral presentation] (20%).
- The final exam [oral group presentation] takes place in class, individually evaluated by one professor. Retakes are permissible, involving the submission of a revised final report and presentation, also evaluated by one professor."

clos.CLO Details: Identify relevant data science techniques for addressing Capstone Project topics.
Formulate clear problem statements and objectives in project proposals.
Plan and execute data collection and cleaning procedures effectively.
Conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA) to uncover patterns and insights in data.
Develop and deploy machine learning models tailored to project requirements.
Evaluate, refine, and optimize machine learning models for improved performance.
Interpret and visualize results effectively to communicate findings to stakeholders.
Summarize conclusions drawn from data analysis and provide actionable recommendations.
Compile comprehensive final project reports integrating insights and methodologies learned throughout the course.
Enhance oral presentation skills through participation in Team Meetings and Final Presentations.

metadata.Learning-Teaching Method: Practice, In-class lecture, Social Constructivism, Active Learning
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries around the world. The aim of this unit is to introduce the current and future applications of AI in trading strategy. Students will be guided to discover the structure used in machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and reinforcement learning (RL) techniques, the required steps, and the optimized methods in the AI-driven trading field. Students also learn how to build some ML models on Keras and Tensorflow.

clos.CLO Details: Understand the fundamentals of trading.
Define quantitative trading and the main types of quantitative trading strategies.
Basic steps in exchange arbitrage, statistical arbitrage, index arbitrage and the application of machine learning to financial use cases.
Design basic quantitative trading strategies.
Use Keras and Tensorflow to build machine learning models.
Build a pair trading strategy prediction model, a momentum-based trading model, and back test them.
Understand the structure and techniques used in reinforcement learning (RL) strategies.
Understand the benefits of using RL vs. other learning methods.
Describe the steps required to develop, test, and optimize an RL trading strategy.

metadata.Learning-Teaching Method: In-class lecture, Social Constructivism, Active Learning
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: Image & Video Processing is an advanced course that covers the fundamental principles, techniques, and applications of image and video processing. The course explores manipulating digital images and videos to extract useful information, enhance visual quality, and perform analysis. It covers various topics, including image acquisition and digitization, image enhancement and restoration, image compression and coding, image segmentation and feature extraction, and object recognition and tracking. The course also covers fundamental concepts in video processing, including video coding and compression, motion estimation, and video analysis. Students will learn to process images and videos using various tools and software platforms, including MATLAB and Python.

metadata.Syllabus Name: GenAI Project_Dự án TTNT tạo sinh
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description:
This capstone project course is designed to consolidate and apply students' knowledge in generative AI and large language models through a substantial team project. Students scope, design, build, evaluate, and present a non-trivial generative AI system or empirical study. Topics applied include:
- The application of generative AI techniques (LLMs, diffusion, RAG, agents, fine-tuning) to solve practical problems.
- The identification and adaptation of generative AI methodologies from current research for specific use cases.
- The development of a comprehensive solution approach using prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning (LoRA / QLoRA), or agent design.
- The evaluation and analysis of generative outputs using appropriate metrics (perplexity, ROUGE, faithfulness, FID, human / LLM-as-judge protocols) and rigorous failure-mode analysis.
- Recognition of appropriate scenarios for prompting vs RAG vs fine-tuning vs agent design.
- Selection of suitable metrics and benchmarks for generative-system evaluation.
- Understanding the ethical, safety, provenance, and legal implications of generative AI (hallucination, bias, deepfakes, copyright, content provenance / C2PA).
- Implementation and reflection on generative pipelines including data preparation, model adaptation, inference / serving, and post-deployment monitoring.
- Effective teamwork and project management across a multi-phase delivery.
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Select a suitable generative AI project and form teams (2-3 members).
- Allocate and schedule tasks among team members.
- Develop a project output that meets the specified requirements and demonstrates individual contribution.
- Submit four progressive reports (Proposal; Data & Baseline; Model & Results; Final Project Report) on time per the schedule.
- Disclose any use of AI tools as required by each report, and be able to explain and defend all submitted work and code.
- Present and defend the project in front of a review panel at the final oral examination.
- Promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
metadata.Tools:
- Programming Languages: Python 3.10+
- Software Tools: Jupyter Notebook / Google Colab, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Diffusers, PEFT, TRL, LangChain, vLLM
- Models: Hosted frontier APIs (Claude, GPT, Gemini) and open-weight families (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek)
- Datasets: Hugging Face Datasets, Kaggle, publicly licensed corpora
- Additional Resources: Papers with Code, arXiv, GitHub, Hugging Face Hub, Weights & Biases for experiment tracking
metadata.Note:
- The essential capstone project is mandatory, focusing on solving a real-world generative-AI problem. It consists of four progressive reports and a final oral presentation.
- The final mark is determined by summing the weighted scores of: Report 1 - Project Proposal (10%), Report 2 - Data & Baseline (20%), Report 3 - Model & Results (30%), Report 4 - Final Project Report (10%), and Final Exam - Oral group presentation (30%).
- The final exam (oral group presentation) takes place in class, individually evaluated by one professor / lecturer or a review panel.
- Completion Criteria: every assessment component > 0 AND Final Exam Score >= 4 AND Final Result >= 5.

Formulate problem statements, scope, objectives, and success criteria in a project proposal.
Plan data preparation, model selection, and licensing/ethics review.
Conduct baseline analysis using pre-trained models, prompting, and in-context learning.
Develop and adapt generative-AI systems to project requirements.
Evaluate and optimize systems using appropriate metrics and protocols, with attention to contamination and saturation.
Interpret outputs and failure modes (hallucination, bias, jailbreak) and visualize results for stakeholders.
Summarize conclusions and actionable recommendations, including deployment and cost/latency trade-offs.
Compile a final report with an explicit ethics, safety, and provenance subsection.
Deliver oral presentations with live demonstrations and Q&A defense.

metadata.Syllabus Name: Advanced MLOps_Hoạt động học máy nâng cao
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: This course provides students with practical knowledge and skills to bridge the gap between machine learning model development and production deployment. Students will master essential Python programming for MLOps, explore the integration of DevOps practices, and build efficient microservices, including the application of high-performance languages like Rust for zero-shot classification. The curriculum covers cloud-based data engineering pipelines using AWS technologies (such as AWS Step Functions, Lambda, and SageMaker) alongside industry-standard tools like MLflow and Hugging Face for model tracking, reproducibility, and deployment. Through hands-on projects, students will gain comprehensive experience in designing, building, and managing end-to-end operational pipelines for real-world AI and ML solutions.
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Students are responsible for completing all exercises, assignments, and labs assigned by the instructor in class or at home, and submitting them on time.
- Laptops are to be used in class strictly for learning purposes.
- Students must promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
metadata.Tools: Python, AWS (SageMaker, Lambda, Step Functions), MLflow, Hugging Face, Rust, GitHub.
metadata.Note:
- The mandatory capstone project focuses on designing, implementing, and deploying an end-to-end MLOps system for a real-world machine learning application. Students progressively develop the project through four milestone reports covering infrastructure design, cloud-based data engineering, model lifecycle management, deployment, and final system integration.
- The final mark is calculated by summing the weighted scores of: Progress Test (10%), Report 1 - Infrastructure & Pipeline Proposal (10%), Report 2 - Data Engineering & AWS Integration (10%), Report 3 - Model Tracking & Deployment (30%), Report 4 - Final System Report & Group Presentation (10%), and Final Exam - Computer-based Multiple-choice Examination (30%).
- The Progress Test is conducted immediately after the completion of Chapters 1, 2, and 3 to evaluate students' understanding of Python programming, software engineering practices, MLOps methodology, cloud infrastructure, and AWS-based machine learning services.
- Reports 1 to 4 are conducted as in-class group presentations with instructor evaluation and immediate feedback. Each report represents a major milestone of the capstone project and assesses students' practical implementation, documentation quality, system architecture, technical presentation, and teamwork.
- The Final Exam is an individual computer-based multiple-choice examination administered by the examination board. The examination comprehensively evaluates theoretical knowledge and practical concepts from all course chapters, including Python foundations, MLOps methodology, cloud platforms, MLflow, Hugging Face, and production deployment. At least 70% of examination questions must differ from those used in previous semesters.
Completion Criteria: every assessment component > 0 AND Final Exam Score >= 4 AND Final Result >= 5.

clos.CLO Details: Understand the core concepts of Python programming, advanced data structures, and their specific applications within MLOps workflows.
Apply clean coding practices, modern testing frameworks, and efficient data manipulation using Pandas and NumPy for machine learning data readiness.
Understand the fundamental principles of MLOps, DevOps, and DataOps methodologies, including their importance in the software development lifecycle.
Design and compose software solutions using microservices architectures and automated operations pipelines to support scalable machine learning applications.
Understand the principles of ethical AI and the application of high-performance languages like Rust for zero-shot classification and efficient processing.
Understand cloud-based data engineering architectures, including data ingestion, repository creation, and secure data transformation solutions.
Apply cloud technologies (such as AWS Step Functions, AWS Lambda, and Amazon SageMaker) to build, monitor, and automate end-to-end data engineering and modeling pipelines.
Understand the fundamentals of MLflow, including the Tracking UI, model registries, and artifact management via APIs.
Apply MLflow and Hugging Face modules to package reproducible machine learning projects and deploy pre-trained models efficiently.
Implement an end-to-end Advanced MLOps project that includes infrastructure setup, automated data pipelines, model tracking, cloud deployment, and reporting.

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6
assessments.Question Type: Computer-based multiple-choice test
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: MLOps foundations, Python engineering standards, testing frameworks, MLOps methodology, cloud ML services (AWS/SageMaker), MLflow experiment tracking & model registry, Hugging Face integration, and infrastructure automation (Chapters 1–4).
assessments.Grading Guide: Conducted in class using the LMS/Computer-based system; automatically graded and reviewed by instructor.
assessments.Note: Test schedule is announced in the Course Implementation Plan. The instructor reviews test results and discusses common mistakes with students. Moved to Slot 45 after theory & hands-on labs.

assessments.Question Type: Written proposal + oral group presentation
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Problem definition, system architecture, MLOps pipeline design, development workflow, technology stack selection, project repository structure, infrastructure planning, and project management strategy.
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS followed by an in-class presentation evaluated using the Proposal rubric.
assessments.Note: AI-use disclosure is mandatory. Instructor provides immediate feedback after presentation.

assessments.Question Type: Technical report + AWS implementation demonstration + oral presentation
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Automated data ingestion, ETL pipeline design, AWS Lambda, Step Functions, SageMaker integration, cloud resource management, data validation, reproducible workflows, and infrastructure deployment.
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS together with source code and demonstrated in class through an oral presentation.
assessments.Note: Cloud resources configuration files, and deployment scripts must be reproducible. Instructor provides immediate feedback after evaluation.

assessments.Question Type: Technical report + working system + live demonstration + oral presentation
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: MLflow experiment tracking, model registry, reproducibility, artifact management, Hugging Face integration, model serving, REST API deployment, production monitoring, project evaluation metrics, and deployment results.
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS together with complete implementation. The live system/REST API and deployment are evaluated using the project rubric.
assessments.Note: AI-use disclosure is mandatory. System must be executable and reproducible. Instructor provides immediate feedback after presentation.

assessments.Category: Report 4: Final System Report & Group Presentation
assessments.Question Type: Final technical report + complete source code repository + documentation + presentation
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Complete end-to-end MLOps solution including infrastructure, cloud deployment, CI/CD pipeline, experiment tracking, model deployment, monitoring, system evaluation, project documentation, limitations, and future improvements.
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS and presented in class. Evaluated by instructor using the Final rubric.
assessments.Note: AI-use disclosure is mandatory. Each team member must provide an individual contribution statement. Complete documentation and reproducibility guideline are required.

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7, CLO8, CLO9
assessments.Question Type: Computer-based multiple-choice examination
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Comprehensive assessment covering MLOps concepts & Python engineering foundations, testing & code quality, MLOps methodology, operations pipelines, cloud platforms (AWS SageMaker), automated data engineering, MLflow tracking/registry, Hugging Face deployment, reproducibility, and production MLOps concepts.
assessments.Grading Guide: Conducted by the examination board on university computer system.
assessments.Note: Examination questions must be updated with at least 70% new questions compared with previous semesters. Individual assessment only.
